basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 7.' and it opens '(Vers. 7.) Maledictus furor eorum, quia procax; et ira eorum, quia dura: dividam eos in'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 7.) Maledictus furor eorum, quia procax; et ira eorum, quia dura: dividam eos in Jacob, et dispergam eos in Israel. Levi enim haereditatem propriam non accepit, sed in omnibus sceptris, paucas urbes ad habitandum habuit. De Simeon vero in libro Jesu scriptum est (Josue XIX), quod et ipse proprium funiculum non fuerit consecutus, sed de tribu Juda quiddam acceperit. In Paralipomenon (I, 4) autem libris manifestius scribitur, quod, cum multiplicatus fuisset, et non haberet possessionis locum, exierit in desertum. Quidam prophetice interfectos homines, Apostolos, et subnervatum taurum a Pharisaeis, Christum interpretantur.
